assessment.nobel_worthiness: Public knowledge supports a very distinctive poetic voice and a sustained project of remaking Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and a critical dialogue with inherited forms. The long career in poetry and essays has had wide significance for modern Arabic writing. Its formal and intellectual ambition is high and fits Nobel's call for work of an idealistic tendency, read broadly.
assessment.attribution: A single-writer citation is straightforward: the renewal of Arabic poetic language and form, with the essays on tradition and modernity as a companion body of work. Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses are representative. The citation should rest on literary achievement rather than the writer's political positions.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre is more than six decades long and has been consistently productive and influential, so the body of work is fully formed. The writer's advanced age makes timing a practical consideration, though it does not establish merit.
uncertainties: Poetry depends heavily on translation, and my knowledge of how well the Arabic's musical and formal qualities survive in Swedish and English is limited.
I have not independently read or verified the sources, and my coverage of the essays and later poetry is uneven.
Public controversy around some of the writer's statements may affect how the work is received, but it is not a literary criterion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visionary, densely patterned prose with a strongly individual voice. Public knowledge supports ambitious works of metaphysical and bodily imagination, including the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid. These show formal range, architectural control and an expansive intellectual project that draws on memory, dream and science.
assessment.attribution: A clear single-author citation would cover the creation of an encyclopedic, metaphysical prose universe from Romanian memory and imagination, with poetry as the early foundation. Blinding and Solenoid are the central works.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre is substantial and has been sustained from poetry through large-scale novels, with strong late work. It is well established in several translations.
uncertainties: The density and length of the major novels make the quality of their translations hard to judge, and my coverage of the Romanian prose rhythms is limited.
The poetry and earlier work are less familiar to me than the major novels.
Some of the imagery is repetitive across volumes, and I am unsure how the committee would weigh that.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Writing in both Japanese and German, she turns linguistic estrangement into a formal principle across fiction, poetry, essays and drama. Her narration is inventive, often witty and philosophically alert. The Emissary and Memoirs of a Polar Bear are representative. Her work is notable for linguistic and imaginative originality rather than scale alone.
assessment.attribution: The citation would cover bilingual and translingual literary invention across genres, with the single named writer clearly identified. The two-language practice is part of the achievement and not merely a biographical fact.
assessment.maturity: The career spans several decades and shows consistent experimentation and development. It is well established in both literary cultures.
uncertainties: Her central effects depend on wordplay between Japanese and German, which I cannot fully assess and which translation into a third language may flatten.
I am less sure about the poetry and drama than about the prose.
I have not independently verified the details of the German-language corpus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large, polyphonic novels that reshape the form through Indigenous sovereignty, oral storytelling structures and ecological time. Carpentaria and The Swan Book show a strongly original voice and ambitious narrative architecture. The work has intellectual depth and a clear claim to contribute something new to world literature.
assessment.attribution: A single-writer citation would address the renewal of the novel through Aboriginal Australian storytelling, politics and landscape, with nonfiction as a secondary strand. The literary method, not its political symbolism, should carry the citation.
assessment.maturity: The body of fiction is smaller than some others on the list, though recent large-scale work suggests continued development. Standing is substantial, though perhaps still consolidating.
uncertainties: The oeuvre is relatively compact, so sustained quality across decades is harder to judge.
Some of the prose is deliberately dense and the committee's reading experience may differ from mine.
I am less certain about the latest work and the nonfiction.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hybrid works of travel, essay and fiction that map Central Europe through borderlands, memory and intellectual history. Danube and Microcosms are representative. The writing has wide erudition, a distinctive essayistic voice and a humanistic breadth of the kind that suits the will. I particularly value its blend of scholarly precision with narrative curiosity.
assessment.attribution: The citation would address the literary essay-narrative as a means of understanding European culture and identity. The writer is clearly identifiable, and his scholarship in Germanistics is part of the context for the literary work.
assessment.maturity: A long, consistent career with a mature and recognizable method. The principal works are already long established.
uncertainties: Erudite, allusive prose may lose texture in translation, and I cannot assess the Italian directly.
The scholarly and journalistic writing may be less literary in the narrow sense, and I am unsure how to weigh it.
Fiction and drama are less familiar to me than the central hybrid works.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A poet of large-scale sequences that turn suffering, landscape and collective memory into memorial form. Purgatory and Anteparadise are known as demanding, ambitious works, and the public interventions extend the poetry into landscape and sky. The voice is distinctive and the work carries significant moral and historical weight.
assessment.attribution: A single-poet citation would cover the poetry of historical trauma and collective memory in Chile and beyond. Distinguishing the textual work from the public art interventions would matter for the scope.
assessment.maturity: The career is long and sustained, with major work dating from the late 1970s onward and continued production since.
uncertainties: Poetry in translation is an acute difficulty, and the visual and performative elements cannot be fully assessed from the text alone.
The political and historical context carries a risk of symbolic rather than literary reading.
My knowledge of the most recent books is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dense, compressed prose that transforms obscure lives and art history into powerful narrative inquiry. Small Lives and The Eleven are widely discussed as formal achievements of language and style. The voice is unmistakable and the work is intellectually and linguistically intense.
assessment.attribution: A clear single-author citation would address the invention of a concentrated prose of lives, memory and art. The oeuvre is small in volume, which is part of its character.
assessment.maturity: The body of work is compact but consistently high in ambition. The compactness makes sustained quality easier to see and breadth harder to claim.
uncertainties: The syntactic compression and register are among the hardest things to translate, so the Swedish and English reception may understate the French.
The limited volume of work may be read as narrower significance by some members.
I have not independently verified the corpus coverage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Uncanny, precise narrative voices that expose exclusion, family power and unstable belonging, across fiction and drama. Three Strong Women and My Heart Hemmed In are representative. The prose is controlled and the imaginative vision is distinctive and disquieting, with real formal command.
assessment.attribution: A single-writer citation would address the estranging narrative of belonging and domination in contemporary French-language fiction and theatre. The scope is clear and the literary method is the center of the claim.
assessment.maturity: The career has been productive since the 1980s and is still developing. The oeuvre is substantial and consistent, though she is younger than many others on the longlist, so timing is less pressing.
uncertainties: Understated, tightly controlled prose can lose some of its effect in translation.
I know the drama less well than the fiction.
Whether the oeuvre has reached its full scope is open to different judgments.
